text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 50

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination on its own — it's common and proves nothing about any individual decision. Led with as your main argument, it reads as insinuation and invites a defensive response.

Your real case is the qualification gap. On paper you have a master's in educational leadership plus five years actually doing the job; he has short courses and no leadership experience. In most jurisdictions, when a visibly less-qualified man is appointed over a woman, the employer must justify it — and silence for two weeks on a lawful request for written reasons is itself a problem.

So: push hard on the written explanation and the comparison. Mention the panel composition once, as context, not as your accusation.
